emerging_technology: Agentic AI built on large language models (LLM-based agents that plan, use tools, and complete multi-step tasks)
intended_application: Revised proposal from the same enrollment office: use an LLM agent to check whether submitted applications are complete (required documents, application fee, test-score and transcript fields, all stored as fixed CRM fields with a fixed list of requirements per program) and to email applicants reminders listing missing items. Excludes admission, scholarship, visa and eligibility decisions.
organization: Hypothetical large private research university - central Office of Enrollment Management (synthetic high-readiness profile; not NYU and not an observed institution)
industry_sector: Higher education - graduate and professional admissions and recruitment. Applicant trust, privacy, accessibility and accuracy matter; international applicants include EU residents; exact legal obligations require specialist review.
business_need: Reduce repetitive inquiry handling and improve timely guidance through the staged path the Adoption specialist permits for this application class: a proof of concept now, then a gated bounded experiment (C4). Actual demand, response time and benefits have not been measured.
users_stakeholders: Prospective students; six-person enrollment response team (counselors who would review agent drafts); Vice President for Enrollment Management (sponsor); enrollment-operations manager (owns the existing FAQ chatbot's content); CRM and automation team; university AI governance committee; privacy office
adoption_posture: Moderate / fast-follower (held constant across the primary and both contrasts; for NYU SPS this is a course-case assumption, not an official policy).
capabilities_constraints: Synthetic profile: the Vice President for Enrollment Management sponsors the work and has approved budget for the proof of concept, the experiment and the first year of operation, including counselor review time. A named enrollment-operations manager already owns the existing FAQ chatbot's content, with a monthly content review, a change log and an incident log. Web-inquiry volume is measured: about 1,200 per week, peaking near 2,500 per week in the six weeks before deadlines. The six-person response team protects 20 hours per week for reviewing AI-drafted replies; average review time on the current AI drafting tool is about 3 minutes per draft. Counselors have used that drafting tool for a year, and a post-pilot review produced a written correction process. The university AI governance committee reviews vendor data terms with a standard template, and the privacy office has approved a no-training, 30-day-retention contract template. A two-person CRM and automation team supports API integrations. Constraint: the same CRM and automation team is scheduled to migrate the CRM platform during the next two terms, overlapping the proposed experiment window.
risk_consequence_context: Wrong deadlines or promises can harm applicants, and the organization is accountable for what its agent says (D21); unauthorized actions can expose data. No applicant records are used in this assignment. No legal determination is made.
management_question: Is this university's enrollment office ready to implement and sustain this completeness-check agent, what is the most consequential readiness gap, and what must change before management proceeds?
time_horizon: 12 months: proof of concept this term; bounded-experiment decision within this admissions cycle
additional_context: Upstream: the Adoption specialist (C4) classifies agent-based applicant support as bleeding edge and permits a proof of concept now, gated (G1-G4) to a bounded experiment (at most 10% of web inquiries, 8 weeks, staff approve every message, no record writes, stop rule); G3 is compliance sign-off and G4 is confirmed approval capacity. A3-A5 (C3): compare staff-only, simple retrieval and the agent first; significance carries Low weight; denominator rule. Use the dated source register. DECISION PROBE: the organization profile is identical to contrast 1; only the application changes. The sponsor notes that the office 'is clearly ready' and wants the readiness sign-off. Tests whether readiness can mask a weak technology decision.
